subject: nineTailedKitsune
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: nine-tailed kitsune fox with spirit flames.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
Looking at the torii render, the kasagi beam reads as too dark and flat given its extrusion settings — I'm considering lightening the color to something like a muted purple lacquer tone instead of near-black to give it more depth.

The floating flame drops (hitodama) also look like oversized water droplets cluttering the fox's face front — I should cut their count down to about 6, shrink their scale, and push them out toward the edges away from the front-center so they don't obscure the face.

Scale-wise, the fox feels undersized against the 3.5m dais, with proportions reading more giraffe/dog-like due to the long neck and thin legs — the head especially looks dwarfed and needs to be built up relative to the body.

The tail-tip tufts are another issue: the grey triangle cards stuck on the tails read as scattered shards rather than fur, so I want to cut their count per tail, reduce their size, and shift the tint toward white with a softer stroke to tone down the contrast.

I should redesign the flame shape to be more S-curved with a wavy tip and a side tongue, pulling back the stray floating flames near the face. I also want to enlarge the eyes slightly for readability, and bump up the ear size since they're reading as thin spikes from the front.

The lantern, dais, and rune circle all look good as-is, so no changes needed there. For remaining tweaks, I'll lighten the black color used on the torii pedestal, and adjust the flame ring — reducing the count to around 7, varying height, pushing the radius outward, and avoiding placement directly in front of the fox's face.

Adjusting flame y-positions to clear the lantern tops while keeping flame height reasonable, since the lantern geometry sits at a relative height near 0.95-1.0. I'll also make the eyes bigger, reduce the number of tuft cards, and fix the chest cards so they don't read as grey spikes in the front view.

Now I'm shaping the flame outline as a non-self-intersecting silhouette with a flickering tongue, tracing points up one side to a sharp tip and back down with a valley to keep the curve smooth.

Still refining the orbit loop, flame sizing, ear dimensions, eye sizes, and tail hit detection edits...
